title: Acme PingFederate → PingFederate
lede: Two PingFederates: Acme is an outside company's IdP and issues the ID-JAG after a sign-in at its own login page; ours is the resource authorization server and redeems it with a JWT bearer grant through an IdP connection. mcp-sample trusts resource-as's tokens only, so step 4 shows a refusal here.

nodes.label: Browser
sub: the playground page · session cookie only
Clicks each step's button
Sees decoded claims and redacted requests, never a raw token

nodes.label: Playground server · the OAuth client
sub: server/ · /api/id-jag-playground
Holds every token server-side: refresh token, ID-JAG, access token
Runs a pre-flight check before each button

nodes.label: Acme PingFederate · issuer
sub: ACME_PF_URL · pf-acme.example.invalid
Its own login page (code + PKCE, offline_access)
Token exchange policy issues the ID-JAG, aud = PF_URL
Signs with the key published at /pf/JWKS

nodes.label: Our PingFederate · resource AS
sub: PF_URL · /as/token.oauth2
JWT bearer grant through an IdP connection to Acme
Client PF_REDEEMER_CLIENT_ID (id-jag-redeemer)
Mints from its access token manager

nodes.label: mcp-sample · MCP server
sub: MCP_URL · POST /mcp
Verifies the token against resource-as /jwks: typ, iss, aud, exp
tools/list shows only what the scope allows

nodes.label: Protected resource
sub: GET /protected/profile on mcp-sample
Same bearer validation as the MCP tools
Says which check failed when it refuses

edges.label: sign-in dialog → /issuer/pi-flow (pi.flow at Acme, code + PKCE, prompt=login)
code → /issuer/callback · server keeps the Acme refresh token
GET /protected/profile → refused, names the failed check
broken assertions: replay · tampered signature · other client · extra scope

steps.title: Sign in at Acme
steps.what: A sign-in at the Acme PingFederate's own login page, separate from this app's sign-in. The server runs code + PKCE against Acme and keeps its refresh token.
steps.why: Two PingFederates on purpose: an IdP must not redeem its own ID-JAG (draft §9.3).

steps.title: Get an ID-JAG from Acme
steps.what: RFC 8693 token exchange at Acme with requested_token_type=…:id-jag, subject = the Acme refresh token, audience = our PingFederate's issuer (PF_URL).
steps.why: Two PingFederates on purpose: an IdP must not redeem its own ID-JAG (draft §9.3).

steps.title: Redeem at our PingFederate
steps.what: RFC 7523 JWT bearer grant at our PingFederate as PF_REDEEMER_CLIENT_ID. Its IdP connection to Acme verifies the signature with Acme's JWKS, then its access token manager mints the access token.
steps.why: Gotcha: PingFederate cannot pick a key by x5t. Acme must publish a single-key JWKS, and our PingFederate caches it: re-save the IdP connection (or restart it) after a key change, or redeem fails with "Invalid JWT token".

steps.title: Call mcp-sample (refused)
steps.what: tools/list and the protected page go to mcp-sample with our PingFederate's token. mcp-sample trusts resource-as's tokens only, so it refuses and names the failed check: the expected outcome in this mode.
steps.why: Our PingFederate minted this access token, and mcp-sample trusts resource-as only, so the MCP call and the protected page refuse it and say which check failed. PingFederate → resource AS shows them accepted.

steps.title: Negative tests
steps.what: Each test mints a fresh ID-JAG at Acme, breaks one thing and expects our PingFederate to refuse it with no token.
